overview: Nyoongar is the indigenous name of the south-west region of Western Australia and experiences six distinct environmental seasons. In contrast to the four European seasons, Nyoongar seasons are not governed by calendar dates, rather, changes in the weather, blooming of flowers, and migration of animals. These seasons are culturally significant to the Nyoongar people as it guides their understanding of nature and connects them to the land. This app aims to help share this understanding and connection to the land by relating these seasons to BoM (bureau of meteorology) daily observation data.
note: the data visualises the data by grouping each season with two months that best represent the time of year they occur. These months do not define clear start and end boundaries of the Nyoongar seasons.

Birak.overview: defined by easing of the rains, sea breeze picks up from the SW and increase in temperature. Also known as a fire season. First nations people would burn the land to aid in seed germination, create easy travel routes, and increase grazing land.

Bunuru.overview: hottest time of the year with minimal rain and easterly winds. This makes it perfect time for living by and fishing at the coast. Bunuru also sees the blooming of many white flowers.

Djeran.overview: temperature begins to decrease with cool nights and dewy early mornings. It represents a time of flying ants and red flowers blooming. Shelters are traditionally repaired to ensure they are waterproofed before the wet seasons.

Makuru.overview: Makuru is the coldest and wettest time of the year. This represented a time to move inland, and diet shifted from costal foods to those of the land. Many animals in this time begin to pair up in preparation for breeding.

Djilba.overview: transitional time of year that combines cold days with warm, rainy, windy days. Defined by a massive blooming period of vivid flowers in the south-west region. As the temperatures begin to rise, newborn animals begin to be born.

Kambarang.overview: shows continued abundance of vivid flowers and rising temperatures. Increased dry periods happen this time of year.
